results.title: GPU cloud cost comparison: H100, H200, L40S per hour
results.author: Cloud Provider Benchmarks Research
highlights:
Published: 6 November 2026 Updated: 6 November 2026 Türkçe oku 

Direct answer

Among the published USD list prices at the access date, the L40S is the lowest-cost GPU per hour and the H200 the highest. Per TB/s of memory bandwidth, however, the published H100 and H200 prices are lower than the L40S. Compare across currencies only after applying current exchange rates and tax treatment.

## Executive summary 

This analysis lists the published on-demand list prices per GPU-hour for H100, H200 and L40S at the tracked providers, each with its source and access date, and normalises them per GB of GPU memory and per TB/s of memory bandwidth. Prices stay in each provider's own currency and billing basis. Several providers offer a GPU without publishing an hourly price; they appear as available but unpriced.

...

1. 01 Prices are published in different currencies (USD and TRY), so no cross-provider ranking is computed on this page.
2. 02 Billing granularity differs: per second with a minimum charge, per minute, or hourly. Short jobs can cost more than the hourly price implies on coarse billing.
3. 03 Some GPUs are offered without public prices (for example PortvMind H200/L40S and several hyperscaler configurations); they are marked as unpriced rather than estimated.
4. 04 Per-GPU-hour list prices exclude storage, data transfer and host resources that some providers bundle and others bill separately.

## Published prices

## Why there is no single ranking

- Currency. PortvMind lists prices in Turkish lira excluding tax; the other providers list in US dollars. Converting at a fixed rate would make the page wrong within weeks.
- Configuration. Some providers sell one GPU per instance; others price an 8-GPU node and the per-GPU figure assumes the full node.
- Billing granularity. DigitalOcean bills per second with a 60-second minimum, PortvMind bills per minute, and Vultr bills hourly. Hetzner bills per started hour with a monthly cap but does not offer these GPU models.
- Bundled resources. vCPU, host RAM and local NVMe are included at some providers and priced separately at others.

results.title: Cloud GPU Pricing: RunPod, Vultr, DigitalOcean, Lambda, AWS
results.author: David Lewin
highlights:
David Lewin · Updated October 18, 2026 · 8 min read

## TL;DR

The bottom line, before the detail

On 23 October 2026 an L40S (48 GB) cost $0.79 to $1.09 an hour on RunPod, $1.57 on DigitalOcean, $1.671 on Vultr and $1.861 on demand on AWS (g6e.xlarge); an H100 SXM cost $2.69 to $3.99 on RunPod, $2.99 per GPU in Vultr's 8-GPU server, $3.99 to $4.29 on Lambda and $6.88 per GPU on demand on AWS (p5.48xlarge). The hourly rate is only half the comparison: billing granularity, storage while stopped, minimum terms and above all the tokens per second you actually get decide the price per job. Rent the candidate GPU for an hour, run the benchmark script in this guide at your real concurrency, and divide.

...

## List prices on 23 October 2026

On-demand prices per GPU per hour, in US dollars, taken from each provider's pricing page or public API on 23 October 2026. Prices change often; the provider's page wins over this table.

| GPU (VRAM) | RunPod Community / Secure | Vultr | DigitalOcean | Lambda | AWS on demand |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 4090 (24 GB) | $0.34 / $0.89 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB) | $0.74 / $0.99 | n/a | $1.57 | n/a | n/a |
| L40S (48 GB) | $0.79 / $1.09 | $1.671 (1 GPU, 16 vCPU, 180 GB RAM) | $1.57 | n/a | $1.861 (g6e.xlarge) |
| A100 80 GB SXM | $1.39 / $1.79 | $2.80 (8-GPU bare metal, $22.40/h) | n/a | $2.79 (8-GPU) | n/a |
| H100 80 GB SXM | $2.69 / $3.99 | $2.99 (8-GPU bare metal, $23.92/h) | $4.41 | $4.29 (1 GPU), $3.99 (8-GPU) | $6.88 (p5.48xlarge, $55.04/h) |
| H200 (141 GB) | $3.59 / $5.29 | n/a | $4.47 | n/a | n/a |

Sources: RunPod pricing page; Vultr's public plans API (`api.vultr.com/v2/plans` and `/v2/plans-metal`); DigitalOcean's GPU Droplet pricing page; Lambda's pricing page (plus sales tax); AWS prices via instances.vantage.sh for us-east-1 Linux. results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in October 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
After a summer of falling floors, October pauses: H100 ~$2/hr, H200 ~$3+, the B200 in-stock floor flat near $3.75 — but a typical on-demand B200 now rents at ~$8. The floor stopped falling.

 By Dex Mareno · claude-sonnet · October 23, 2026 

The takeaway

- As of late October 2026, the cheapest reliable on-demand H100 (80GB) is back around $1.99/GPU-hr (Voltage Park), with brand-name specialty clouds at ~$2.50 (Hyperstack PCIe), ~$2.89 (RunPod), and ~$2.90 SXM (Ori); the median 'cheapest' across two dozen providers is ~$3.33, and spot dips to ~$0.94 (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler H100 is still ~$10–13/hr.
- H200 (141GB) firmed since September: neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99 (Prime Intellect ~$3.14, Spheron ~$3.35, Theta ~$3.69, Hyperbolic ~$3.99), the Ornn transacted index settled at $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 is ~$7.91–13.78.
- B200 (Blackwell) is the split-screen card: the verified in-stock on-demand floor is ~$3.75 (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70 — but the on-demand MEDIAN is now ~$7.99–8.19 (RunPod $7.99, Together $8.19). Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr).
- The October story is that the floor stopped falling: after a summer of monthly cuts, floors across all three cards are flat-to-firmer.
- And the spread that matters moved inside the specialty market — the ~2× gap between a marketplace in-stock rate and a brand-name neocloud's on-demand list price is now sharper than the old specialty-vs-hyperscaler framing for anyone who can tolerate the availability risk.
- The decision is still utilization, not sticker: below ~40–50% duty cycle a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.

...

| GPU | Cheapest reliable on-demand | Typical on-demand (median) | Hyperscaler on-demand | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (80GB) | ~$1.99/hr (Voltage Park), ~$2.50 PCIe (Hyperstack) | ~$3.33/hr | ~$10–13/hr | 70B-class inference, most fine-tunes |
| H200 (141GB) | ~$3.14/hr (Prime Intellect), ~$3.35 (Spheron) | ~$5.00–5.24/hr | ~$7.91–13.78/hr | Bigger context, larger models on one card |
| B200 (Blackwell) | ~$3.75/hr in-stock (Packet.ai) | ~$7.99–8.19/hr | ~$14–16/hr | Frontier-size inference, heavy training |
| GB200 / B300 | ~$8/hr and up, much is quote-only | varies widely | ~$16–27/hr | Largest models, frontier training |
| Spot / preemptible | ~$0.94/hr H100, ~$2.29 H200, ~$3.20 B200 | no SLA | rarely offered | Interruptible batch jobs |

...

## The price map (published on-demand rates, late October 2026)#

Every figure below is a published on-demand rate, gathered the last week of October 2026 from public pricing pages and multi-provider trackers (getdeploying, Ornn, gpuperhour, Spheron, and vendor pages). GPU pricing moves weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read this for the shape of the market, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.

- H100 (80GB) — the workhorse, and steady. The cheapest reliable on-demand rate is back near $1.99/hr (Voltage Park), with ~$2.50 PCIe at Hyperstack, ~$2.89 at RunPod, and ~$2.90 SXM at Ori. The median "cheapest across providers" is ~$3.33. Spot dips near $0.94/hr (Prime Intellect). Hyperscaler on-demand: ~$10–13/hr — the same card, 5–6× the money.
- H200 (141GB) — more memory, and firmer than September. Neocloud floors run ~$3.14–3.99/hr (~$3.14 Prime Intellect, ~$3.35 Spheron, ~$3.69 Theta, ~$3.99 Hyperbolic). The Ornn transacted index — settled daily from real neocloud deals — printed $5.24 on Oct 12, and getdeploying's on-demand median is ~$5.00 across 33 providers. Spot ~$2.29. Hyperscaler H200 runs ~$7.91–13.78 (Thunder Compute: AWS ~$7.91–9.89, Azure ~$10.60–13.78).
- B200 (Blackwell, 180GB) — the split-screen card. The cheapest verified in-stock on-demand rate is ~$3.75/hr (Packet.ai, per getdeploying on Oct 22) — essentially flat versus September's ~$3.70. But the on-demand median is now ~$7.99–8.19: RunPod lists $7.99/hr and Together ~$8.19/hr. Spot from ~$3.20 (Vultr). Hyperscaler B200 is ~$14–16/hr.
- GB200 / B300 — the Grace-Blackwell superchips remain premium and partly quote-only: roughly $8/hr and up where published, ~$16–27 at the hyperscalers. If you need one, you're negotiating, not shopping a list.

results.title: GPU Cloud Prices October 2026: H100, A100, L40S Across 16 Providers
results.author: Bo Shen
highlights:
We collected on-demand GPU list prices from 16 cloud providers three times a day from October 7 to 19, 2026. List prices barely moved: 14 of 407 tracked offers changed. The spread between providers is the real story: H100 from $2.99 to $13.98 per GPU-hour (4.7×), A100 2.6×, L40S 2.1×. And 13 of 22 H100 listings didn't say whether the card is SXM, PCIe or NVL, a difference worth 2.25× in served tokens in our tests.

...

Since October 7 we've collected on-demand GPU list prices three times a day: 42 snapshots so far, about 370 offers from 16 providers. Sources: the Lambda, DigitalOcean and Vultr APIs, and NVIDIA Brev's public catalog, which covers AWS, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, Nebius, Crusoe, Hyperstack, Massed Compute and others. The live table is on our GPU prices page.

...

Of 407 offers we tracked across the period, 14 changed price at all:

- One real on-demand cut: an 8×A100 offer from Excess Supply dropped from $3.60 to $1.62 per GPU-hour on October 10 (−55%).
- Back and forth: Google Cloud's 8×H100 alternated between $12.41 and $13.98 per GPU-hour, and its T4 offers moved by about 1%. This looks like the catalog reporting different regions on different days rather than price changes.
- Spot prices moved more: DigitalOcean's spot price for AMD MI355X rose from $2.97 to $5.50 per GPU-hour (+85%), MI350X from $2.46 to $3.50 (+42%), and NVIDIA B300 fell from $8.00 to $6.17 (−23%).

On-demand list prices behave like price lists, not markets: they change in steps, rarely. Whatever is moving in GPU pricing week to week (availability, spot and marketplace prices, negotiated discounts) doesn't show up in the list.

## Where you rent matters far more

The same GPU model costs very different amounts depending on the provider. Taking each provider's cheapest on-demand offer per GPU-hour on October 19:

| GPU | Providers | Cheapest | Median | Most expensive | Spread |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | 11 | $2.99 (Vultr) | $3.56 | $13.98 (Google Cloud) | 4.7× |
| A100 | 10 | $1.62 (Hyperstack, Massed Compute, Excess Supply) | $1.98 | $4.18 (Google Cloud) | 2.6× |
| L40S | 9 | $1.06 (Massed Compute) | $1.86 | $2.23 (AWS) | 2.1× |
| H200 | 3 | $4.47 (DigitalOcean) | $4.80 | $6.48 (Nebius) | 1.4× |
| AMD MI300X | 2 | $2.59 (DigitalOcean) | $3.29 | $3.99 (Vultr) | 1.5× |

The big clouds sit at the top of each range. Most of the market clusters well below them: eight of eleven H100 providers list between $2.99 and $4.41.

...

These are list prices at collection time for on-demand capacity. They exclude storage, egress, reserved and committed-use discounts, and they don't tell you whether capacity is available: most offers in the catalog carry no availability flag. Brev's catalog reports one region per offer, which can change between snapshots. Twelve days is a short window. RunPod and peer-to-peer marketplaces where hosts set their own prices aren't included.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing 2026: Cheapest Rate per GPU | GPU Cloud HQ
highlights:
# GPU cloud pricing: the cheapest published price for every GPU

What one GPU costs for a month at 30 clouds and hosts, read from their own pricing pages: the lowest price, the median and the highest, GPU by GPU — next to our flat monthly price. Across the 10 GPUs we rent, ours is 33–64% below the median, and the lowest published price of all for 6 of them.

- Prices read on 15 October 2026
- Hourly rate × 730 h, or the provider's monthly price
- Standard on-demand tiers — no spot, no preemptible

## Cheapest published price, GPU by GPU

One GPU, one month. Each provider's figure is its standard on-demand rate kept running for 730 hours, or its listed monthly price; the cheapest one is named with its conditions. Click a GPU for every provider's price, or a provider for the full comparison.

| GPU | Cheapest published | Lowest, a month | Median, a month | Ours, a month | Ours vs median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 288 GB HBM3e · 9 providers publish it | Massed Compute: $52.80/h for 8× B300 — $6.60 per GPU-hour | $4,818 | $6,563 | $3,790 21% under the lowest | −42% |
| NVIDIA B200 180 GB HBM3e · 11 providers publish it | Vultr: $3.50/GPU/h for an 8× HGX B200 instance | $2,555 | $5,745 | $2,690 5% over the lowest | −53% |
| NVIDIA H200 141 GB HBM3e · 15 providers publish it | Leaseweb: CA$2,481.65/mo ($1,747) — 1× H200 NVL 141 GB (PCIe), Montreal | $1,747 | $3,862 | $1,690 3% under the lowest | −56% |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM 80 GB HBM3 · 24 providers publish it | Voltage Park: from $1.99/h for a single H100, no contract | $1,453 | $2,628 | $1,249 14% under the lowest | −52% |
| NVIDIA A100 80 GB HBM2e · 18 providers publish it | Vast.ai: median $0.51/h, SXM4 (14 Oct) · offers from $0.40 | $372 | $1,455 | $649 74% over the lowest | −55% |
| NVIDIA L40S 48 GB GDDR6 · 14 providers publish it | Novita AI: $0.55/h | $402 | $1,139 | $429 7% over the lowest | −62% |
| NVIDIA L4 24 GB GDDR6 · 8 providers publish it | Vast.ai: median $0.20/h (15 Oct), 7 offers | $146 | $475 | $169 16% over the lowest | −64% |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB GDDR7 ECC · 14 providers publish it | Leaseweb: CA$1,142.10/mo ($804) — 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Montreal | $804 | $1,639 | $749 7% under the lowest | −54% |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090 32 GB GDDR7 · 5 providers publish it | Salad Cloud: $0.50/h High priority · $0.25 batch | $365 | $540 | $279 24% under the lowest | −48% |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 24 GB GDDR6X · 6 providers publish it | Novita AI: $0.33/h · $0.17 spot | $241 | $281 | $189 22% under the lowest | −33% |

Highlighted rows: our monthly price is the lowest published price for that GPU. Prices in USD excluding VAT; providers that price in euros, pounds or Canadian dollars are converted at the rate stated on their comparison page. Spot, preemptible and community tiers are cheaper still where they exist and are listed on each provider's page. Read on 15 October 2026 — prices change without notice, every figure links to its source.

## Hourly or monthly: where the line falls

An hourly GPU is cheaper when it is switched off most of the month. Below, the number of hours a month under which the lowest published hourly rate costs less than our flat price — above it, the monthly server wins.

| GPU | Lowest hourly rate | Our monthly price | Hourly is cheaper below |

| B300 | $6.60/h · Massed Compute | $3,790 | 574 h a month 79% of the month |
| B200 | $3.50/h · Vultr | $2,690 | Even 24/7 |
| H200 | $3.62/h · Massed Compute | $1,690 | 467 h a month 64% of the month |

Hours = our monthly price ÷ the lowest published standard on-demand hourly rate for the same GPU. Where that rate wins even around the clock, it usually comes from an open marketplace of third-party hosts or with a multi-GPU minimum — the provider's page says which. Our price is a dedicated, single-tenant server with its CPU, RAM, NVMe and 20 TB of transfer included.

...

On 15 October 2026, 24 providers published a price for the H100. Kept running for a month, the cheapest comes to $1,453 (Voltage Park), the median to $2,628 and the most expensive to $8,972 (Microsoft Azure). A dedicated H100 SXM server is $1,249 a month here, and an 8-GPU node $7,990.

How much do the B200 and H200 cost to rent?

# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.
